description:
A New Ice Cream Calculator ? Is it any good?

In this video, I’m introducing a new ice cream calculator developed specifically for easy ice cream recipe development. 

This is the website for those that want to try it: https://scoopulator.app/

With enough comments and likes, I will do a full useage video next week showing the entire process of developing a FULL recipe. 

This isn’t a recipe video — there’s no base formula to follow here. Instead, this is about understanding and controlling ice cream formulation using a calculator that helps balance key variables like solids, sweetness, and overall structure.

I walk through:
 • What the calculator is designed to do
 • How to use it effectively
 • How it helps remove guesswork from ice cream development
 • Why formulation-first thinking leads to better, more repeatable ice cream

Whether you’re experimenting at home or refining recipes more seriously, this calculator is meant to help you think like an ice cream formulator, not just follow instructions.

This video will continue to evolve, and future videos will build on it with real-world applications and examples if you show interest. Let me know in the comments ok!

⸻

Tags / Keywords
Polar Ice Creamery, ice cream calculator, ice cream science, ice cream formulation, ice cream ratios, frozen dessert science, ice cream development, ice cream solids, sweetness balance, ice cream texture

comments.text:
I fixed the goopy Allulose problem.  I use 60% Allulose and 40% Splenda. Scoops beautifully and has great texture. Tastes great too.

Using Patrik's calculator I formulate my ice cream using only sugar. When making the mix I factor the sugar by .6 to determine the grams of Allulose to use. I then convert the remaining grams of sugar to cup measurements and add Splenda accordingly. It's a couple of extra steps, but the end product is really worth it.

My ice cream is 5% fat and nearly sugar free. I do add some corn syrup to improve texture. The corn syrup also makes up for Allulose being only 70% as sweet as sugar.
comments.author: @garyrobbins6280

comments.text: ​​ @garyrobbins6280 Splenda supposedly is worse than sugar, healthwise, except for the glucose hit you get from sugar. Might want to try Monk Fruit or Stevia and reformulate.
